I'm working out that the rule checks each nonzero cell's four orthogonal neighbors (left, right, up, down), treating out-of-bounds cells as zero, to determine if any neighbor is zero.

Now I'm tracing through a specific 14x13 grid example, checking a shape occupying rows 0-3, columns 1-5, colored 1, to see how border cells behave under this padding logic.

So for each cell, the up/down/left/right neighbor comparisons check whether "0" appears in the string form of that neighboring row list, deciding whether to keep the original value or replace it with 8 — since every row in this grid contains a zero somewhere, most border cells end up preserved rather than overwritten.

This effectively means the rule is a simple erosion: a nonzero cell becomes 8 only if all four of its neighbors are also nonzero, treating anything outside the grid as zero. Neighboring cells of different colors still count as "nonzero" for this purpose, so I'm tracing through each shape (A, B, C, D) to mark their interior cells as 8 while leaving their edges as-is, including checking where shape D touches the grid's border.

Continuing the grid rows, I'm filling in the remaining interior sections with the 2 and 3 bordered blocks, checking that rows 7-10 form the second box and rows 8-12 form the third box with 8s inside, then closing everything with the final zero and border row.
